children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Adani Green Energy (AGEL) on Wednesday reported a net profit of 747 crore for the quarter ended September, up 16% from 644 crore a year earlier. Total income rose 39% to 4,520 crore from 3,249 crore. The renewable energy arm of Adani Group posted a 33% year-on-year increase in energy sales in the first half of FY27 to 12,090 million units, supported by a 24% expansion in greenfield capacity.

Revenue from power supply in the first half rose 36% year-on-year to 8,299 crore, while Ebitda grew 41% to 7,957 crore, enabling an industry-leading Ebitda margin of 93%. "If curtailment would not have been there, Ebitda would have been close to 9,000 crore," said Ashish Khanna, CEO of AGEL. In a statement, the company said its operational capacity grew 24% YoY to 20.8 gigawatts (GW) in the first half, putting it on track to achieve its 50 GW target by 2030.

AGEL added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity on a YoY basis during April-September, including 2,957 MW of solar capacity, 805 MW of wind capacity and 321 MW of solar-wind hybrid capacity in Khavda, Gujarat. For the September quarter, the company's cash profit rose 45% to 1,951 crore from 1,348 crore a year earlier.

Energy sales increased 33% to 12,090 million units during the quarter, reflecting the impact of its expanding operational capacity. Segment wise, revenue from power supply, the company's main business, increased 45% YoY to 4,019 crore from 2,776 crore, driven by the commissioning of new solar, wind and hybrid projects.

title: Adani Green Energy Posts 16% Rise in Q2 Net Profit
